advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Guard the criteria-scaled floor computation so a criteria-less non-bug ticket (which `explicit_completion_criteria` rejects) falls back to a default floor instead of aborting verification.
evidence: src/rebar/llm/completion.py:571: `step_floor = verify_step_floor(len(explicit_completion_criteria(root)), verify_cfg)`
src/rebar/llm/completion.py:567-570 try/except wraps only `_config.load_config`, NOT the criteria call, so a raise from `explicit_completion_criteria` propagates out of `_verify_completion_inner`

src/rebar/llm/workflow/completion_recovery.py:100-104: `raise CompletionRecoveryError("cannot enumerate completion recovery criteria for a non-bug ticket without explicit acceptance-criteria checkboxes")`
tests/unit/workflow/test_completion_recovery_contract.py:38-39 pins that a `task` ticket without checkboxes raises `CompletionRecoveryError`
docs/llm-framework.md:710: `a ticket with no explicit criteria PASSes with a note.`
advisory.finding: `_verify_completion_inner` now calls `explicit_completion_criteria(root)` unconditionally to size the criteria-scaled step floor, but that helper RAISES `CompletionRecoveryError` for a non-bug ticket with no Acceptance-Criteria checkboxes. This aborts verification before the workflow runs, breaking the documented graceful 'no explicit criteria PASSes with a note' behavior for task/story/epic tickets that lack checkbox criteria.
scenarios: Closing/verifying a task or story whose description has no `## Acceptance Criteria` checkboxes (or only prose criteria) — previously a graceful PASS, now a hard CompletionRecoveryError at the gate.
advisory.suggested_fix: Wrap the `explicit_completion_criteria(root)` call in a try/except CompletionRecoveryError (or reuse a non-raising count) and fall back to `verify_step_floor(0, verify_cfg)` / the packaged default so criteria-less tickets still reach the workflow's graceful-PASS path.

dropped.checklist_item: - [ ] Treat a whole-file read returning exactly `cap` lines as complete (or detect completeness from a real EOF signal) so the exactly-cap boundary is memoized rather than re-read.
evidence: src/rebar/llm/agent_call.py:227: `entry = {"lines": wlines, "max": cached_max, "complete": cached_max < cap}`
src/rebar/llm/pai_tools.py:64: `hi = min(hi, lo + _READ_MAX_LINES - 1)` — a file of exactly cap lines returns all cap rows with none truncated, yet `cached_max == cap` makes `complete` False
src/rebar/llm/agent_call.py:206-209 `_servable`: `return entry["complete"] or bool(le and le <= entry["max"])` — a whole-file re-read (le=0) of an exactly-cap file is not servable
ABSENCE: tests in test_agent_call_memo_nudge.py cover >cap (truncated) and <cap files but not the exactly-cap boundary
dropped.finding: The whole-file read cache marks an entry complete via `cached_max < cap`, so a file whose length is EXACTLY `_READ_MAX_LINES` (a full, non-truncated file) is misclassified as truncated. `_servable` then returns False for a whole-file re-read (le=0), forcing an exact fallback read and defeating the memo for exactly-cap-length files.
scenarios: A read_file call returning exactly _READ_MAX_LINES rows; every subsequent whole-file or beyond-cap re-read re-executes the underlying tool instead of serving from cache.

dropped.checklist_item: - [ ] Confirm the intended behavior when an operator explicitly sets REBAR_LLM_MAX_STEPS to exactly DEFAULT_MAX_ITERATIONS (250): it is now conflated with the default and can lower the completion-verifier budget below the prior 480 floor.
evidence: src/rebar/llm/completion.py:572: `if cfg.max_iterations == DEFAULT_MAX_ITERATIONS or cfg.max_iterations < step_floor:`
Old behavior (removed): `if cfg.max_iterations < _VERIFY_MIN_STEPS:` with `_VERIFY_MIN_STEPS = 480` — a pure min-only raise that lifted 250 to 480

src/rebar/llm/config.py:127: `DEFAULT_MAX_ITERATIONS = 250` — so an operator's explicit `REBAR_LLM_MAX_STEPS=250` is indistinguishable from the framework default and is treated as 'no explicit budget'

Consumer: `REBAR_LLM_MAX_STEPS` is a documented public env var (docs/llm-framework.md:401, docs/config.md:321); the CI job that sets `REBAR_LLM_MAX_STEPS: "900"` (.github/workflows/jira-dc-capability-map.yml:105) still wins, but an explicit 250 would now yield a smaller verifier budget than before
tests/interfaces/contracts/test_completion_budget.py:66-77 confirms a 1-criterion ticket at the default is now lowered to 48 (was raised to 480)
dropped.finding: verify_completion's step-budget resolution changed from a pure min-only raise to `cfg.max_iterations == DEFAULT_MAX_ITERATIONS or cfg.max_iterations < step_floor`, which conflates an operator who EXPLICITLY set `REBAR_LLM_MAX_STEPS=250` with the unset default and now LOWERS the completion-verifier budget below the previous flat-480 floor for that value (previously any value <480, including 250, was raised to 480).
scenarios: An operator who deliberately pinned REBAR_LLM_MAX_STEPS=250 for the completion verifier now silently gets the criteria-scaled floor (as low as 48) instead of the prior 480 budget.
